message.reasoning_content:
We need to determine appropriate criminal charge(s) for the facts.

Facts: In Wuhan, a person (谢某) under influence of drugs, hallucination, used a lighter to set bedding on fire in a dormitory (宿舍) that he was staying in (or maybe a rented unit). The fire destroyed property worth 4040 yuan (air conditioner, bed, etc.). He fled, was caught.

Potential charges: arson (放火) or "非法点燃火源致人死亡或重伤"? Actually Chinese criminal law: Article 114 (放火罪) - "故意放火，危害公共安全的行为". Also "过失放火罪"? He intentionally set fire (though under drug influence). So likely "放火罪" (arson). Also maybe "非法占有他人财物"? No, he didn't steal. He caused property damage. Could be "故意毁坏财物罪"? But arson is more severe. The typical classification: "放火罪" (arson). In Chinese law, "放火罪" is under Article 114. The description: "以燃烧、爆炸、投掷、投放等手段，放火毁坏公共财物或者他人财物，致使公共安全受到危害的行为". So yes.

Thus answer: [罪名]放火<eoa>

Check examples: earlier they used "放火" as "放火" or "失火"? In earlier examples, they used "失火" for accidental fire (due to negligence). For intentional fire, they used "放火". Example: earlier "刘某甲携带火纸、打火机...因烧火冥纸不慎将山林引燃" they labeled "失火". That was accidental. Here it's intentional (though under drug hallucination). So "放火". Also maybe "非法持有毒品"? He was using drugs, but the charge is about fire. The case may also include "吸毒" but not necessarily a crime (drug consumption is not a crime). So only "放火".

Thus final answer JSON.
